This appeal by the appellant/claimant u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 23.08.2004 passed by First MACT, Dabra, District Gwalior (M.P.) (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.01 of 2004 whereby Claims Tribunal has rejected the claim petition filed by appellant/claimant on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.
2.
Brief facts of the case are that on 01.05.2003, appellant along with his friend Ajay Verma came to Gwalior on a Jeep bearing No.M.P.07 H 4682.
Appellant was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, due to which, the vehicle overturned near Murari Village.

As a result of which,
appellant suffered multiple injuries on his right hand, shoulder, head and back and a cut on the right hand.
Ajay Verma also sustained injuries.

Appellant was brought to J.A Hospital, Gwalior for treatment where he was admitted and his preliminary NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20583 2 MA-972-2004 treatment was started.

In the X-ray examination,
fracture was found in the bone of the left hand of appellant.
A report was lodged in this regard at Police Station, Bilaua, Gwalior on the basis of which, a case under Section 60/2003 was registered.
After investigation, Charge-sheet has been filed before the Competent Court.

Therefore,
appellant/claimant filed claim petition before the Claims Tribunal under Section 163-A of Motor Sachin Kumar Jain vs Bhupendra Kumar And Ors.

3. Counsel for respondents filed their written statements and thereafter, Claims Tribunal framed the issues after recording the evidence of both the parties rejected the claim petition.
4. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, appellant filed this appeal and submitted that the award passed by the Claims Tribunal is arbitrary and contrary to law.
The Claims Tribunal has not considered the evidence adduced by the appellant/claimant.
It is further submitted that police has registered the case and submitted charge-sheet after investigation against the Driver of the offending vehicle.

Driver and Owner of the offending vehicle are unable to adduce any evidence before the Claims Tribunal in their favour, therefore, Claims Tribunal has committed an error in rejecting the claim petition.

Hence, it is prayed that the impugned award be set aside and amount of Rs.1,00,000/- be enhanced as compensation in his favour.
5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of this appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the entire record.
7.

It is true that if the claimant has been able to demonstrate NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20583 3 MA-972-2004 satisfactory and cogent reason for delay in lodging the F.I.R. then delay in lodging F.I.R. should not be treated as fatal for such proceeding.

The Apex Court in case of Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and Others AIR 2011 SC 1226 in para 20 and 21 has held as under:-
20.

entities.text: Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and Others AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay,
the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered toimplicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
21. The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.

2 of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

8. In the present case, accident occurred on 01.05.2003 and according to the pleading of appellant/claimant/injured, immediately after the accident, he NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20583 4 MA-972-2004 was admitted in J.A Hospital, Gwalior, where his preliminary treatment was done.
He was admitted in the said hospital for 8 to 9 days.

It was pleaded by him that he informed the treating Doctor S.S.Jadon that he had sustained injuries in motor accident, but on perusal of the record, it appears that appellant has not produced any documentary evidence regarding his treatment at J.A.Hospital Gwalior and appellant was also unable to examine the treating Doctor, namely, S.S. Jadon before whom appellant had informed about the injuries received by him in the alleged motor accident.
It is also pleaded that according to Ex.P-11, he was also treated by Dr. Satyendra Kumar Sharma, but in Ex.P-11, it is not mentioned that injuries received by claimant was a result of road accident.
In Ex.P-10 also, it is nowhere mentioned that the injuries sustained by appellant, were a result of road accident.

9. It is settled principle of law that if police files charge-sheet after investigation against the driver of the offending vehicle, Tribunal can presume that accident was done by driver of the offending vehicle but thus presumptions should be rebuttable.

It is also settled principle of law that mere delay in lodging the FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case, but it is the duty of claimant to explain as to how and in which manner, the delay has been caused in lodging the FIR.
10. In the present case, it is the duty of the claimant to explain delay in lodging the FIR.

According to claimant, accident occurred on 01.05.2003, but as per FIR, he informed the police station on 10.05.2003 i.e. after nine days and claimant gave the reason for lodging delayed FIR that he was admitted in hospital for treatment and after recovery, he came to report, but, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20583 5 MA-972-2004 appellant was unable to adduce any documentary evidence before the Claims Tribunal in order to show that he was admitted in hospital from 01.05.2003 to 09.05.2003.
Claimant was also unable to adduce any documentary evidence regarding medical treatment in order to show that his treatment was done in J.A.Hospital, Gwalior.
In documents (Ex.P-10 and Ex.P-11), it is nowhere mentioned that claimant has sustained injuries due to road accident.
11. So, due to lack of documentary evidence, the case of claimant creates suspicion/doubt about the alleged accident caused by Driver of the offending vehicle.

12. In view of the aforesaid discussion and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, false implication of offending vehicle for seeking compensation cannot be ruled out, therefore, Claims Tribunal has not committed any error in rejecting the claim petition filed by appellant.
Accordingly, the appeal being devoid of merits, is hereby dismissed.
Sachin Kumar Jain vs Bhupendra Kumar And Ors.
